title: Value-density and discovery-economics audit for latent older-adult human assets
objective: Determine whether the hidden older-adult asset pool is economically dense enough to justify repeatable high-touch discovery outside publicly subsidized community infrastructure.
truth_rules: PROFESSIONAL ROLE DENSITY != EVERYDAY TACIT-ASSET DENSITY
AGGREGATE ECONOMIC BENEFIT MAY BE CONCENTRATED
DISCOVERY FRICTION EXISTS != DISCOVERY BUSINESS EXISTS

observed_density_classes.name: role-legible / demand-legible professional capability

evidence.fact: Chongqing reports 1,019 retired high-level/high-skill talents serving基层 in 2025, with 1.1 million patient visits, 540 teaching classes, 7,000+ training/consulting service instances and about RMB200 million direct economic benefit.
Nan'an used 39 retired cadres/party members as dedicated mediators; in 2024 the system handled 572 disputes with a 92% success rate.

An older Chongqing clinician has been rehired for more than ten years and individually accumulated 30,000+ patient consultations, showing very high repeated use when capability and use-case are explicit.

observed_density_classes.interpretation: When capability is already legible and tied to a recurring demand category, utilization can be extremely high. In these cases the main problem is not discovering hidden everyday value; ordinary professional labor-market/credential mechanisms already identify the asset.

observed_density_classes.name: credentialed talent pools with explicit demand routing

evidence.fact: Fujian's silver-talent platform received 3,098 online service requests and matched 3,028 by Feb 2026, reporting a 97.7% matching success rate.
A current Guangdong plan targets about 200 silver technology experts serving around 100 enterprises/research institutions, and 300 silver medical experts with at least 200 actually serving基层.
evidence.evidence_role: planned utilization target, not achieved result

observed_density_classes.interpretation: Once both the role and demand are explicit, matching may be operationally tractable. This weakens the thesis that a universal source-legibility layer is the main bottleneck for credentialed assets.

observed_density_classes.name: large talent pools with opaque member-level utilization

evidence.fact: Quanzhou reports 3,126 silver talents in the pool and 500+ volunteer-service events serving nearly 50,000 people, but public reporting does not identify how many unique talents were active or how activity is distributed.
Zhejiang reports 48,324 silver talents and 559 brand teams/workshops, but the public aggregate does not expose active/dormant member rates.
Hunan reports 131 silver-talent pools and 23,000 managed talents without a comparable individual utilization denominator in the same report.

observed_density_classes.interpretation: Pool scale is easy to report; individual activation density is often not. Public evidence does not justify treating every listed person as callable or repeatedly useful.

observed_density_classes.name: explicit underutilization / role-activation gap

evidence.fact: A 2026 Liancheng inspection rectification item explicitly addressed 'silver talent role not obvious'. The pool had 208 members; rectification highlighted 6 rural-revitalization specialists and 12 community party-role participants, plus new targeted mapping and contact work.
evidence.caution: The report does not state that only 18 of 208 were active; it is evidence of an official underutilization problem, not a computed activation rate.

evidence.fact: Shaoxing reports 5,100+ retired cadres in its pool but still needs concentrated mapping and demand interviews to convert this into 52 service-supply projects and nearly 100 identified demand recipients at city level.
evidence.caution: A service-supply project is not equivalent to one active talent; no member-level activation rate should be inferred.

observed_density_classes.interpretation: Database membership does not guarantee that useful, current and requested capability has been activated.

observed_density_classes.name: ordinary/tacit craft capability with repeated social + market use

evidence.fact: The Beijing Silver Artisan project reports 42 incubated older artisans, 72 market events, 800+ public classes, 3,000+ works sold and aggregate artisan income above RMB250,000; the highest individual reported increase was nearly RMB30,000.

Fengtai's broader Silver Workshop has nearly 200 older artisans/retired experts across 38 community pilots, but current public reporting emphasizes activation and market linkage rather than a comparable aggregate income/utilization denominator.

observed_density_classes.interpretation: Everyday/non-credentialed capability can generate repeated classes and product sales, but current monetary capture is materially lower and more uneven than high-demand professional roles. Social/cultural value may be large while private economic surplus remains modest.

evidence.fact: Silver Artisan reports aggregate income above RMB250,000 across 42 incubated artisans while the top individual reached nearly RMB30,000, indicating non-uniform capture even within a selected successful cohort.
Broad 50+ digital-author participation is large but current reporting notes commercial returns remain limited for many.

concentration_warning.implication: A large source pool can coexist with power-law or low-median economics.

evidence.fact: Successful public systems commonly rely on government/community staff, service stations, volunteer organizations, free/low-cost venues, insurance and program funding.

public_subsidy_and_infrastructure_effect.implication: Observed output cannot be translated directly into private discovery economics without pricing the discovery/trust/space/coordination infrastructure.

reasons: many public reports do not expose active/dormant ratios
clear high-density value clusters are dominated by credentialed roles already legible to existing systems
ordinary/tacit assets show real repeated use but weaker/uneven monetary capture
community infrastructure subsidizes discovery and trust
discovery_economics_inference.stronger_pattern: VALUE DENSITY RISES WHEN A RECURRING USE-CASE / DEMAND CLASS IS ALREADY LEGIBLE
discovery_economics_inference.caution: This is a cross-case inference, not a measured causal law.

reasoning: capturing capability at retirement preserves employer/role/context before it disappears
current government practice already uses one-person-one-file / retirement registration linkage

evidence.fact: Current public programs link retirement procedures/records to silver-talent registration and build one-person-one-file profiles.

transition_capture.unknown: No current evidence quantifies discovery-cost savings or downstream private value from transition capture.

decisive_verdict.core_update: The main formation is no longer 'discover all hidden older-adult assets'. Value appears highly heterogeneous. A sustainable layer, if one exists, likely needs selective/event-triggered or use-case-informed activation rather than expensive blanket supply mapping.

contradiction_to_current_formation.statement: If the only economically dense assets are credentialed capabilities with already-legible recurring demand, then LATENT HUMAN-ASSET LEGIBILITY is not a broad private missing edge; existing professional/talent systems already solve the valuable portion.

next_action: Audit whether selective/event-triggered activation can preserve the formation. Focus on retirement-transition capture, use-case-informed discovery and social referral mechanisms that reduce discovery cost without requiring blanket community mapping. Compare whether these mechanisms surface everyday/tacit assets that existing professional systems miss and whether activated assets then receive repeated downstream use. Kill the broad formation if economic density remains concentrated only in already-legible professional roles.
